policies.title: Sensitive tables are only reached by logged-in endpoints
policies.statement: Any endpoint, message handler, AI tool or task that reaches a pii-tagged table, such as one holding customer emails, must call record_audit_event unconditionally in its own stack, so every change to customer data leaves a who-changed-what row in audit_log. Endpoints that reach these tables must also require a login. A call made through another function, or inside a conditional, does not count. Exempting an object is the policy owner's decision.

warnings.text: table_tags "pii" is on no table in this workspace, so no access to it is judged.

policies.title: Tables holding confidential data are tagged
policies.statement: Every table that stores a customer email address carries the pii tag, so the audit and access policies can find it. Tagging is the owner's decision, because tags decide which policies apply. A table whose email field has another name is not covered until its field name is added to field_names by the owner.

policies.title: AI agent calls are not made inside loops
policies.statement: An AI agent run must not sit inside a foreach, for or while loop, because one loop can multiply the model bill without a limit. Batch the work, or move the call out of the loop with a stated item cap. An object that must loop over AI calls on purpose is the policy owner's decision: exempt it with the except_tags only after they approve.

policies.title: External calls are not retried inside while loops
policies.statement: An outbound request (api.request) must not sit inside a while loop. A retry loop with no attempt cap can run forever and keep billing or hammering a vendor. Retry a bounded number of times with a for loop or a counter, or move the retry into a separate function with a stated limit. Changing a retry loop is a code change the owner approves.
